properties.trigger: any competition in football (soccer) at any level; a position, stat key, stage, card, suspension, walkover, formation, table, transfer or tiebreaker question in that sport
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, stat_line

data.short_description: Football (Soccer): association football at every level, from Sunday-league, club, youth and small-sided football to the professional game and fantasy football. Positions, stat keys, stages, standings and tiebreaker presets, roster and registration rules, officials, forfeits, discipline, youth data defaults, a glossary, and what the amateur, professional and fantasy levels each change.

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
This pack is association football, called soccer in some countries; human-facing text says football (soccer), or football once the context is set. Sport code: soccer (a bare football code would be ambiguous next to american_football). It covers every level in one vocabulary: Sunday-league and adult-league sides, clubs with several teams (first team, reserves, over-35s), youth club teams, small-sided and futsal leagues, a local league the owner merely follows, the professional and international game, and fantasy football. The Recreational, Professional and Fantasy chunks say what each level changes; the required chunks hold what is true everywhere. Three workflow rules sit on the pack: rule/soccer_matchday_log (a side the owner plays for or runs, and a league they follow), rule/soccer_club_campaign (a professional club across its competitions in one season) and rule/soccer_transfer_window (professional roster moves).
A match is called a match, game or fixture. It has two halves of 45 minutes at 11v11 (shorter halves or four quarters in small-sided and youth football; two 20-minute stopped-clock halves in futsal). Cup ties may add extra time (two halves) and a penalty shootout. The single score number is goals: home_score and away_score are goals after extra time, excluding shootout kicks. Draws exist and are common; result draw, never tie.
Default competition: format league, scoring_system 3-1-0 (3 points for a win, 1 for a draw, 0 for a loss); level recreational for amateur adult football, youth for age-group football, pro or semi_pro for paid football, international for national teams, fantasy for fantasy leagues. A cup is a second competition with format knockout (or group_knockout), scoring_system win_loss. The form of the game is the competition's match_format: 11v11 (the default), 9v9, 7v7, 5v5, futsal, walking, indoor; an event's match_format overrides it (a futsal tournament inside a club season). The same word is also a tag on the competition, so one tag search finds every small-sided league.
Every entity in this sport carries the tag soccer. Positions, stat keys, stages, decided_by values and officials below are the only ones to use; anything else goes to Extended keys first.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Position codes for PLAYS_FOR.position, secondary_positions and PLAYED_IN.position. Use the most specific the owner gives; GK, DF, MF, FW are fine when they only say "defender".
GK: goalkeeper.
CB: centre-back.
LB: left-back. RB: right-back.
LWB: left wing-back. RWB: right wing-back.
SW: sweeper (older systems; rare).
DF: defender, unspecified.
CDM: defensive or holding midfielder.
CM: central midfielder.
CAM: attacking midfielder or number 10.
LM: left midfielder. RM: right midfielder.
MF: midfielder, unspecified.
LW: left winger. RW: right winger.
ST: striker or centre-forward.
CF: second striker or false nine, when the owner distinguishes it from ST.
FW: forward, unspecified.
Small-sided and futsal roles: GK (futsal goalkeeper), FIXO (futsal defender), ALA (futsal winger, left or right), PIVO (futsal target player), UTIL (utility, plays anywhere; common in 5v5 and 7v7 where roles rotate).
Formations go on COMPETED_IN.formation as digits from the back, outfield players only: 4-4-2, 4-2-3-1, 3-5-2; 7v7 2-3-1 or 3-2-1; 5v5 1-2-1 or 2-2; futsal 1-2-1 or 2-2.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
season.stage and event.stage values, at every level: preseason (friendlies before the first competitive match), friendly (a non-competitive match at any time of year), exhibition (a charity or festival match), qualifying (qualifying rounds before a main draw or a tournament proper), regular_season (league matches), league_phase (a single-table phase of a continental or cup competition that feeds a knockout), group_stage (cup or tournament groups), knockout (any cup round before the quarterfinal; round names it), knockout_playoff (a two-legged tie between a league phase or group stage and the round of 16), round_of_32, round_of_16, quarterfinal, semifinal, third_place, final, super_cup (a one-match super cup), playoff (end-of-season play-offs in leagues that have them), playoff_semifinal and playoff_final (promotion play-offs), relegation_playoff, play_in, wild_card, round_one, conference_semifinal, conference_final (a post-season bracket with conferences; its cup final is stage final), offseason (season stage only, between the last match and the next season).
round, as the league writes it: "Matchday 14" for league fixtures and league-phase matchdays ("Week 14" only when the league itself counts weeks); "Round 1", "Preliminary Round", "Third Round" for cup rounds; "Leg 1", "Leg 2" for two-legged ties; "Game 2" in a best-of series; "Group B Matchday 2" in a group stage; "Replay" for a replayed match ("Third Round Replay" when the cup names its rounds, so the round stays identifiable). A weekend tournament inside a season is a parent event (event_type match, stage group_stage or knockout, end_date) with each game PART_OF it; each side's COMPETED_IN edge to the parent carries that tournament's group, seed and final_rank.
decided_by values: regulation (the match_format's normal time; the default, and may be left blank), extra_time, penalties (a shootout after a draw), golden_goal (older cups), aggregate (a two-legged tie settled on the total), away_goals (two-legged ties in competitions whose House rules chunk keeps the rule), seeding (a level two-legged tie where the higher seed goes through), walkover (the opponent did not fulfil the fixture), awarded (the league overturned the on-pitch result, typically for an ineligible player; the on-pitch score goes in score_display), drawing_of_lots, coin_toss (only if the league truly does it).
Shootouts: home_score and away_score are the goals after extra time, shootout kicks excluded; score_display carries the shootout ("2-2 (4-3 pens)", "1-1 aet (5-4 pens)"); result is home_win or away_win for the side that won the shootout, never draw, even though the goals are level. This is the one case where equal scores are not a draw. For W-D-L records a shootout match counts as a draw, and the AI says so when it quotes one; the event's result exists to answer who went through.
A replay is not a decided_by value: the replayed match is a new event with round "Replay" that names the original in lore (Forfeits and abandonments).

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
All counting stats are stored as integers per match on match-scope lines; season and career lines are their sums unless the owner types a total. Use null for not recorded. Only the rate stats marked stored are ever stored.

PLAYER - appearances and time
appearances: matches in which the player was on the pitch at any point (unused substitutes are not appearances). Season and career lines only; on a match line use PLAYED_IN instead.
starts: matches started.
sub_appearances: appearances off the bench.
minutes_played: minutes on the pitch, on the player's match line. Because the pack lists this key, PLAYED_IN.minutes stays empty in this sport; the edge carries only when they came on and went off. Season value is the sum of match lines, or typed in by the owner when match lines are not kept. Rolling subs: total minutes across all stints.
unused_sub: 1 when named in the squad and did not play (match lines); count on season lines.

PLAYER - attacking
goals: goals scored (penalties included, shootout kicks excluded, own goals excluded).
assists: final pass or cross leading directly to a goal, as the team awards them.
penalty_goals: goals from penalty kicks in normal or extra time.
penalties_missed: penalty kicks in normal or extra time that did not score (saved, wide, post).
penalties_won: fouls drawn that produced a penalty kick for the team.
free_kick_goals: direct free-kick goals.
headed_goals: goals with the head.
own_goals: own goals conceded (count against the scorer; credited to the opponent's team goals, not to any opponent player).
shots: shots attempted. shots_on_target: shots that would have gone in without a save or block.
hat_tricks: 3 or more goals in a match (match line 1 or 0; season count).
braces: exactly 2 goals in a match.
shootout_goals: shootout kicks scored. shootout_misses: shootout kicks not scored.

PLAYER - goalkeeping
clean_sheets: matches where the keeper played the whole match (or was on when all of the team's defensive time passed) and the team conceded none. Two keepers in a 0-0: the one who played more minutes gets it, unless the league states otherwise.
goals_conceded: goals conceded while on the pitch.
saves: saves made.
penalties_saved: penalty kicks saved in normal or extra time.
shootout_saves: shootout kicks saved.
gk_minutes: minutes played in goal (for an outfielder who went in goal after a red card).

PLAYER - discipline
yellow_cards: cautions.
red_cards: dismissals of any kind (straight or second yellow).
second_yellow_reds: dismissals that were a second caution (a subset of red_cards; the match line then has yellow_cards 1 or 2 as the league records it, red_cards 1, second_yellow_reds 1).
straight_reds: dismissals without a prior caution (subset of red_cards).
sin_bins: temporary dismissals (10 minutes for dissent in leagues that use them).
fouls_committed: fouls given against the player. fouls_suffered: fouls won.

PLAYER - other
player_of_match_awards: Player of the Match awards received (season and career lines, derived from WON edges with title Player of the Match; the WON edge is the truth).
captain_appearances: matches as captain on the day (derived from PLAYED_IN.captain).
goals_per_90: derived, never stored. goals * 90 / minutes_played.
goal_contributions: derived, never stored. goals + assists.
shot_conversion: derived, never stored. goals / shots.
save_percentage: derived, never stored. saves / (saves + goals_conceded).

TEAM (match lines are optional; the score lives on the event)
goals_for, goals_against: on season lines, from the event scores. Not stored on match lines.
possession_pct: stored when the owner has it (rare at this level).
shots, shots_on_target, corners, offsides, fouls_committed, yellow_cards, red_cards: team totals for the match when the owner tracks them.
clean_sheet: 1 or 0 on a team match line; clean_sheets on season lines.
failed_to_score: 1 or 0 on a team match line; season count.
own_goals_for: opponents' own goals that counted for this team.
See Standings for the season-line keys. Optional advanced keys for the professional game (expected goals, progressive passes and the like) are listed in the Professional (continued) chunk; a key defined here is never redefined there.

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Team season line keys (scope season, subject_kind team, RECORDED_IN the season, STAT_OF the team): played, wins, draws, losses, goals_for, goals_against, goal_difference (goals_for - goals_against; stored on the season line as a cache even though derivable, because every table shows it and filters sort on it), points (3*wins + 1*draws unless the competition's scoring_system says otherwise), points_deducted (league sanctions, as a positive number; points above is after the deduction), clean_sheets, failed_to_score, and the split keys some tiebreakers read: home_wins, home_draws, home_losses, away_wins, away_draws, away_losses, home_goals_for, home_goals_against, away_goals_for, away_goals_against, disciplinary_points (counted from player match lines with the preset's weights). form is not stored; it is derived from the last five COMPETED_IN results as a string like WWDLW when asked. Head-to-head is never stored; it is computed from the matches between the tied teams.
What counts: every completed, forfeited or awarded match with stage regular_season (or group_stage or league_phase inside its own table) whose two teams both COMPETES_IN the season. Friendlies, cup ties and play-offs never count in the league table. Walkover goals (3-0) count towards goals_for and goals_against unless the competition's House rules chunk says the league records a walkover as points only; then add the points, leave the goals out, and say so in the table footnote. Abandoned matches with result no_result count nothing; if the league let the score stand, the owner changes status to completed. A suspended match counts on the date it was completed.
Columns to show, in order: Pos, Team, P, W, D, L, GF, GA, GD, Pts. Add a footnote for deductions, walkovers and matches in hand (a team with fewer P than the leader).
Default tiebreakers (the preset gd_first), used when the competition's House rules chunk names no other: 1 points; 2 goal_difference; 3 goals_for; 4 head-to-head points between the tied teams; 5 head-to-head goal_difference; 6 fewer disciplinary points (yellow 1, red 3) if the league uses them; 7 a play-off or the league's decision, which you state as unresolved. Name the tiebreaker that split any tied pair.
Tiebreaker presets. Leagues disagree about how to split level teams, so a competition names one of these in its House rules chunk ("tiebreakers: h2h_first") or writes its own ordered list there, which overrides the preset. Each preset starts after points. Apply the steps in order and restart from the top whenever a step reduces the tied group; "h2h" means computed only from the matches among the tied teams:
- gd_first (the default; most leagues worldwide): goal_difference, goals_for, h2h points, h2h away goals, play-off match if a title, relegation or qualification place depends on it.
- gd_first_deep: goal_difference, goals_for, h2h results, h2h goals_for, h2h away goals, overall away goals, play-off.
- h2h_first: h2h points, h2h goal_difference, overall goal_difference, goals_for, play-off for a title, relegation or qualification place.
- h2h_first_minitable: h2h points, h2h goal_difference (two teams: over both matches; three or more: a mini-table among the tied teams, applied only once every pair has met twice), overall goal_difference, goals_for, fair play.
- continental_group (group stages of continental club and national-team competitions): h2h points, h2h goal_difference, h2h goals_for, then the h2h steps repeated among the still-tied subset, then overall goal_difference, goals_for, wins, disciplinary_points, confederation coefficient (the owner supplies it), drawing of lots.
- continental_league_phase (a 36-team single-table league phase): goal_difference, goals_for, away_goals_for, wins, away_wins, points of opponents faced, goal difference of opponents faced, goals of opponents faced, disciplinary_points (red 3, yellow 1, second yellow 3, players and officials), club coefficient. Steps 6 to 8 need every team's results, so with a partial log stop at step 5 and say so.
- world_tournament_group (world tournaments for national teams and for clubs): goal_difference, goals_for, h2h points, h2h goal_difference, h2h goals_for, fair play points (yellow -1, second yellow -3, straight red -4, yellow then straight red -5), drawing of lots.
- wins_first (a conference league, within a conference and overall): wins, goal_difference, goals_for, disciplinary points per match (lowest wins; the league's own weights, which the owner supplies), away goal_difference, away_goals_for, home goal_difference, home_goals_for, coin toss or drawing of lots.
- short_season (apertura and clausura tables): goal_difference, goals_for, h2h result, away goals, fair play, drawing of lots.
Regulations change yearly, so a preset is a starting point the owner confirms. When a step needs numbers the stored lines do not hold (disciplinary points with no card lines, opponents' records in a partial log), stop there, present the teams as tied in that order and name the missing step; never fall through to a guess. Ranking stops at a drawing-of-lots or coin-toss step: report "lots" and keep the order the owner gives. When presenting a table always name the preset used and the step that split any tied teams.
Promotion and relegation: at season end set COMPETES_IN outcome promoted or relegated (also champion, runner_up; playoffs for a play-off place) and final_rank; the next season's COMPETES_IN group is the new division. A league with several divisions is one competition with group on COMPETES_IN naming the division ("Division 2"); a league with conferences puts the conference in COMPETES_IN conference and the division, if any, in group; the table is computed per group, and per conference when the competition has them.
A league the owner only follows: when the owner types in the published table, each team gets a season line with source official, as_of the date of the table, and the match events need not exist. Never rebuild a source official or owner line from COMPETED_IN edges; report it with its as_of and offer to update it. Youth leagues that publish no table: log the results and compute a table only when the owner asks, and say the league does not publish one.

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Squad: at 11v11 a matchday squad is 11 starters plus named substitutes (3 to 7 at amateur level; up to 9 or 12 named with 5 substitutions in three windows at professional level, see Professional). Many amateur leagues allow rolling (repeat) substitutions, so a player can go off and come back on. Record the total minutes as minutes_played on the player's match line (PLAYED_IN.minutes stays empty in this sport) and the stints as text in entered_at and left_at ("30', 75'" and "55', 90'"). A player who went off and was replaced carries replaced_by (the incoming player's slug) and left_at; a substitute who later made way for the player they replaced carries temporary true. No reason for any substitution is ever recorded. Youth and small-sided football nearly always use rolling subs with equal-time guidance; do not police minutes.
Registration windows exist at every level (transfer windows for professionals, sign-on cut-offs for amateurs). Most grassroots leagues require a player to be registered (signed on) with the club before playing, with a cut-off late in the season (often late winter or early spring in a northern-hemisphere season) after which no new signings can play competitive matches. Before adding a PLAYS_FOR edge mid-season, read the season's roster_deadline property if present, else the Season calendar chunk on the season; if the date has passed, log the player and say the league may not allow them to play. Cup-tied players (played in the same cup for another club this season) belong in a lore note on the person.
Club with several sides: the club is a team with team_type club that never COMPETES_IN; each side (First Team, Reserves, Over-35s, U12 Blues) is its own team, team_type club (youth sides too), PART_OF the club, and COMPETES_IN its own competition's season. A player's PLAYS_FOR goes to the side they are registered with; the club's roster is shared across its sides (rule/recording_a_match), so a one-off appearance for another side is a PLAYED_IN edge with for_team that side and no new PLAYS_FOR unless the owner says they have moved up. Season stat lines are per side: a player with lines for two sides in one season has two lines, and the club-wide total is their sum, shown with the arithmetic.
The player-manager: PLAYS_FOR with position plus STAFF_OF role manager (or captain_organiser when they also collect subs and book pitches). Captain: PLAYS_FOR role captain; vice_captain likewise.
Team sheet check before logging a lineup: every player on a side's lineup has an open PLAYS_FOR edge on the match date to that side, to the club it is PART_OF, or to another side of the same club; eleven or fewer starters at 11v11 (seven at 7v7, five at 5v5 and futsal); at most one GK on the pitch at a time. Ringers (not registered, played anyway): PLAYS_FOR arrangement substitute, started and ended on the match date, and a lore note; never pretend they were registered. A player genuinely trialling for a place is arrangement trial.
Trials, academies and transfers between clubs happen at this level too: a player moving club mid-season is an event transfer with no fee (fee "none" or "free"); a youth player moving to a pro academy is a transfer with the receiving club as to_team, nothing more.

lore.title: Officials
lore.content: OFFICIATED.role values: referee (the match official; at grassroots sometimes a club member or a parent), assistant_referee (qualified linesman or lineswoman), club_assistant (a club volunteer running the line, usual in amateur football), fourth_official (cup finals and professional matches), var and avar (video assistant referee and assistant, professional only), reserve_assistant_referee (professional), referee_observer (assessor watching the referee), match_delegate (the competition's delegate at a professional match), match_secretary (the league or club official who confirmed the result; only if the owner names them). Record officials only when the owner names them; names only, no contact details. Video-review decisions (an overturned goal, an awarded penalty) are story, in a lore chunk on the match titled VAR, never a stat key. Professional referees are public people whose names may be recorded as given. Many grassroots referees are teenagers: if the owner says a referee is under 18, is_minor rules apply.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content: No extended keys yet. Add one line per key below, dated, in the form: YYYY-MM-DD key_name: meaning (who asked).

lore.title: Recreational
lore.content:
What amateur, Sunday-league, club and youth football change. Stats are kept sporadically: a result with scorers and cards is a complete record; lineups and minutes only when the competition is tagged lineups-tracked; never ask for numbers nobody kept. Shorter games (2x40, 2x35, quarters), rolling subs (minutes_played on the match line, stints as text in entered_at and left_at), the player-manager, ringers and no-show walkovers are all normal and covered in Roster rules and Forfeits and abandonments. Co-ed (mixed) leagues may require a minimum number of each sex on the pitch and sometimes count goals by one group double: that is scoring_system custom with the rule in the competition's House rules chunk, and a stat line never records a player's sex; the owner checks the lineup rule themselves.

Small-sided forms. Set match_format on every competition (11v11, 9v9, 7v7, 5v5, futsal) and tag it with the same word. Vocabulary is unchanged; what differs:
7v7 and 9v9: formation with 6 or 8 outfield digits (2-3-1, 3-2-3), rolling subs, often 2x25 or 2x30 minutes or 4 quarters. Standings as 11v11 unless the league publishes none.
5v5 and futsal: rolling subs with no limit, 2x20 (futsal, stopped clock) or 2x25 running. Futsal has accumulated fouls (team key fouls_committed; the sixth foul gives a 10-metre penalty), kick-ins instead of throw-ins, and a five-second rule; no offside. Some adult 5v5 leagues award 3 points for a win and a bonus point for scoring 5 or more, or use 3-1-0 with a "sin bin" for dissent: scoring_system custom and the detail in House rules; the Standings chunk's points formula then follows that chunk.
Walking football (over-50s, over-60s): match_format walking, same vocabulary; running is a foul (fouls_committed), no goalkeeper area entry, head-height rule; typically 6v6, no tables in many leagues.
Indoor leagues with boards: match_format indoor; venue indoor true, surface as the owner says (3g, astro, sports_hall). Venue surface values for this sport: grass, 3g (third-generation artificial turf), astro (sand or water-based artificial), sports_hall, concrete.

Club structure. The model is in Roster rules (a club team that never plays, each side its own team PART_OF it). The club team also holds the club's officials: chairperson as STAFF_OF role president, secretary role other with title Secretary, treasurer role treasurer, welfare officer role other with title Welfare Officer, name and role only. Each side is named "<Club> First Team", "<Club> Reserves", "<Club> Over-35s", "<Club> U12 Blues", with short_name as people say it ("the Ressies", "the Vets"). HOME_VENUE belongs on the sides when they play at different grounds, on the club when they share one.
A one-team Sunday side needs no club entity: it is a team with team_type recreational and that is all. Create the club umbrella only when a second side appears, and then re-parent the first side with PART_OF (never rename it).

Match fees. Amateur sides collect match fees (subs) and this world keeps money light. If the owner wants a note, it goes in a lore chunk on the match titled Match fees, in their words ("£5 each, Dan and Jamie owe"), and nowhere else: never a property, never a stat key, never on a person entity, and no running totals computed across matches. Anything more (annual subs, kit money, pitch hire) is a treasurer's spreadsheet, not this world; say so once if asked.

lore.title: Professional
lore.content:
What the top level of football (soccer) adds to the vocabulary above. Positions, the single score number (goals), draws, the 3-1-0 scoring system, the stages, the decided_by values and the Stat keys are unchanged; at every level a match is a fixture of two 45-minute halves plus stoppage time. Professional competitions carry the sport code soccer and level pro or international. Two workflow rules go with this chunk: rule/soccer_club_campaign (one club across several competitions in one season, the matchday routine, the per-competition House rules chunk, international breaks, manager changes) and rule/soccer_transfer_window (windows, fees, loans, contracts, squad numbers, roster mechanics of salary-budget leagues).

FORMATS a professional competition takes (competition.format):
- league: a national league with one table (a top flight, a second division). Promotion, relegation and continental qualification are outcomes on COMPETES_IN.
- league_playoffs: a table then a bracket. A conference league with a post-season cup; short seasons of the apertura/clausura kind (two per calendar year, each a table then a play-off "liguilla"); a second division whose play-off decides the last promotion place (the play-off is PART_OF the same season); and the continental club competitions since 2024-25 (a 36-team single-table league phase, then a knockout play-off round and a bracket).
- group_knockout: the world tournament for national teams, the continental championships for national teams, the world club tournament, the continental cups that still run groups, and regional cups between neighbouring leagues' clubs.
- knockout: domestic cups (the national cup, the league cup) and one-off super cups (one match, stage super_cup).
- exhibition: a friendlies container (pre-season tours, mid-season friendlies, international friendlies), so friendlies hang off a season and never enter any table.
Each competition is its own entity with its own seasons; a club in the top flight, the national cup, the league cup and the continental club competition in 2026-27 has four COMPETES_IN edges to four seasons. Qualifying rounds (continental Q1 to Q3, world-tournament qualifying) are either early-stage matches of the same season (stage qualifying) or, when the owner follows them closely, a separate competition "<Tournament> qualifying". Reserve, B and under-21 or under-23 sides are their own team PART_OF the senior club, in their own competitions.

ROUNDS at this level: domestic cup rounds before the quarterfinal are stage knockout with round written exactly as the competition names it ("First Round", "Third Round", "Fifth Round"), and a replay is "Third Round Replay". League and league-phase matches are "Matchday 11", never "Week 11". Two-legged ties are "Leg 1" and "Leg 2", a best-of-3 is "Game 2", a group stage is "Group B Matchday 2".

RESULTS beyond a single match:
- A knockout match level after 90 minutes follows the Stages and rounds chunk: goals after extra time in the score fields, the shootout in score_display, result the side that progressed, decided_by penalties; a shootout match is a draw for W-D-L records.
- Two-legged tie: one event per leg (round Leg 1, Leg 2; the home side of each leg is that leg's home side) PART_OF a parent event for the tie (event_type match, stage of the round, name "<A> v <B> — <Round> (two legs)", neutral_site true, home_score and away_score the aggregate, score_display "3-3 agg, Rovers win 4-2 on pens" or "4-3 agg", decided_by aggregate, extra_time, penalties, away_goals or seeding, result the side that progressed). Whether away goals still count is a house rule on the competition (the European confederation dropped the rule from 2021-22; some confederations and cups keep it); never apply away goals unless the competition's House rules chunk says so.
- Best-of-3 series (the first round of a conference league's post-season): a parent event with score_display "2-1" and one child event per game (round Game 1 to Game 3) per rule/recording_a_match; in that round and the wild card a level game goes straight to penalties with no extra time, so decided_by penalties and never extra_time.
- Continental club competitions since 2024-25: one season, stage league_phase for the 8 matchdays (36 teams in one table, each plays 8 different opponents, 4 home and 4 away; no groups, so COMPETES_IN group is blank), then knockout_playoff (two legs, 9th to 24th), round_of_16, quarterfinal, semifinal, final (single match, neutral). The top 8 go straight to the round of 16 (COMPETES_IN seed = league-phase position). A supporter who logs only their club's matches has a partial league-phase table: give the club's points and position only if the owner supplies the rest, never a fabricated table.
- Abandoned matches at this level are resumed from the minute of stoppage (status suspended, one event), replayed in full (a new event with round Replay) or awarded (status completed, decided_by awarded), per Forfeits and abandonments.

STANDINGS at the professional level: the Standings chunk's keys and columns apply, but the tiebreaker order is a house rule per competition, because leagues disagree. Every professional competition carries a lore chunk titled House rules with a line "tiebreakers: <preset or ordered list>" naming one of the Standings chunk's presets (gd_first, gd_first_deep, h2h_first, h2h_first_minitable, continental_group, continental_league_phase, world_tournament_group, wins_first, short_season) and, where relevant, "away_goals: yes/no", "conferences: <names>", "qualification: top 4 continental, 5th secondary continental, bottom 3 relegated"; rule/soccer_club_campaign has the procedure. With no House rules chunk, order by points only, mark tied teams as unsplit and ask which preset to use; never guess.

SQUADS, NUMBERS, CAPTAINS: pro squads are registered per competition (a typical top flight: 25 named players over 21 with a home-grown quota; the continental competitions: a List A of 25 with locally trained minimums and a List B for under-21s; salary-budget leagues: a senior roster of about 20 plus supplemental places up to about 30). The squad is the PLAYS_FOR edges open on the date; registration lists per competition are not modelled, note them in lore on the team titled Registration if the owner cares. jersey_number is the squad number for the season, 1-99; a change gets a dated line in a lore chunk on the person titled Squad numbers (the edge keeps only the current number). role captain for the club captain, vice_captain for the deputy, and PLAYED_IN captain true for whoever wore the armband on the day, which can differ. Five substitutions from up to nine named (plus one in extra time) is the modern norm; concussion substitutes exist in many competitions and are recorded as an ordinary substitution (left_at, replaced_by) with no reason.

MANAGERS AND STAFF: the boss is STAFF_OF role manager (title "Head Coach" where the club uses it), with the backroom as assistant_coach, coordinator (set-piece coach), trainer (goalkeeping coach, unit goalkeeping), director (sporting director, title "Director of Football"), analyst, scout, president, owner. A sacking, resignation or departure by mutual consent: end the edge on the date, open the interim's or successor's edge, log one event with event_type staff_change named "<Club> — manager change — <date>", INVOLVED_IN the outgoing person role subject with detail "sacked", "resigned" or "mutual consent", the incoming person role subject with detail "appointed" or "interim", the club role from_team. Compensation and contract length go in detail or lore; nothing personal beyond what the club announced.

lore.title: Professional (continued)
lore.content:
Continues the Professional chunk: national teams, tournament shapes, the conference league, and the modern stat keys.

NATIONAL TEAMS: a national side is a team with team_type national, country set, in competitions with level international (the world tournament, continental championships, a nations league, qualifying, friendlies). A player is on their club and their country at once: a second open PLAYS_FOR edge to the national team with arrangement representative, started at the first cap, position as for the club. Call-ups are not events; a cap is a PLAYED_IN edge on the international match, and the national-team record is a season line RECORDED_IN the international competition's season with for_team the national side (one season line per team, per rule/stats). Dual nationals who switch association: end the first national edge, open the second. A player retiring from international football ends the national edge only. Club matches do not take place during an international window; rule/soccer_club_campaign covers the break.

TOURNAMENT SHAPES to expect: the world tournament for national teams from 2026, 48 teams, 12 groups of 4 (COMPETES_IN group "Group A" to "Group L"), top two plus the eight best third-placed teams to a round_of_32, then round_of_16, quarterfinal, semifinal, third_place, final; preset world_tournament_group. The European championship for national teams, 24 teams, 6 groups of 4, four best thirds to a round_of_16; preset continental_group. The South American championship, 16 teams, 4 groups. The world club tournament (from 2025), 32 teams, 8 groups. A nations league: tiers A to D with groups, promotion and relegation between tiers as COMPETES_IN outcome, a finals in June. Qualifying groups are seasons of a "<Tournament> qualifying" competition with group on COMPETES_IN. Short seasons of the apertura/clausura kind are two seasons of one competition per calendar year (label "Apertura 2026", "Clausura 2027"), each a 17-matchday table then a play-off (play_in, quarterfinal, semifinal, final over two legs with aggregate and decided_by seeding).

A CONFERENCE LEAGUE: one competition (level pro, format league_playoffs, scoring_system 3-1-0), about 30 clubs, COMPETES_IN conference "Eastern Conference" or "Western Conference" (group stays blank unless the league also has divisions), 34 regular-season matches each. Two standings are read from the same season lines: the conference table (preset wins_first) and the overall table for the regular-season trophy (WON title "Regular-season champion" to the season). Post-season: the top 9 per conference (seed on COMPETES_IN); seeds 8 and 9 meet in the wild_card (single match, higher seed hosts, level after 90 goes straight to penalties); round_one is best-of-3 (1 v 8/9, 2 v 7, 3 v 6, 4 v 5; higher seed hosts games 1 and 3; no draws, no extra time, penalties after 90); conference_semifinal and conference_final are single matches with extra time then penalties, higher seed hosts; the final is a single match hosted by the finalist with the better regular-season record, WON title "Champion" to the season. The season runs on a calendar year (label "2026"); matches have a local kickoff and timezone, and the league's broadcast arrangements go in a lore chunk titled Broadcast on the season, not in properties. Roster mechanics (designated players, under-22 slots, homegrown players, allocation money, international slots, the college draft) are in rule/soccer_transfer_window; the base holds them as PLAYS_FOR designation and INVOLVED_IN detail text. Verify the post-season shape against the current season's regulations; such leagues change it often.

PROFESSIONAL STAT KEYS (optional; store only from a source the owner names, with the line's source import or official). They add to the Stat keys chunk and never redefine one of its keys (shots, shots_on_target, saves, goals_conceded, penalties_saved, fouls_committed, fouls_suffered, yellow_cards, red_cards, second_yellow_reds, straight_reds, possession_pct and the derived save_percentage are already there):
Attacking: xg (expected goals, decimal), npxg (non-penalty xG), xa (expected assists), xgot (expected goals on target, post-shot), big_chances, big_chances_missed, big_chances_created, key_passes, touches_in_box, offsides (player).
Possession and passing: passes_attempted, passes_completed, progressive_passes, progressive_carries, progressive_passes_received, final_third_passes, passes_into_box, crosses_attempted, crosses_completed, long_balls_completed, through_balls, touches, carries, dribbles_attempted, dribbles_completed, dispossessed, miscontrols.
Defending: tackles, tackles_won, interceptions, blocks, clearances, recoveries, aerials_won, aerials_lost, duels_won, duels_lost, errors_leading_to_shot, errors_leading_to_goal, defensive_contributions (clearances + blocks + interceptions + tackles, plus recoveries for midfielders and forwards where the fantasy game counts them).
Goalkeeping: psxg (post-shot xG faced), penalties_faced, sweeper_actions, passes_launched, claims, punches.
Fantasy bonus: bps (the official fantasy game's bonus-points-system score), bonus_points.
Team: xg_for, xg_against, shots_for, shots_against, corners_for, corners_against, ppda (passes allowed per defensive action, stored), field_tilt_pct (stored), big_chances_for, big_chances_against.
Derived, never stored: pass_completion_pct = passes_completed / passes_attempted * 100; shot_accuracy_pct = shots_on_target / shots * 100; xg_per_shot = xg / shots; goals_minus_xg = goals - xg (player) or goals_for - xg_for (team); xg_difference = xg_for - xg_against; dribble_success_pct = dribbles_completed / dribbles_attempted * 100; per_90 for any counting key = key / minutes_played * 90, always stated with the minutes it covers. Expected-goal numbers differ by provider, so a season xg line records its provider in source_url or a lore chunk titled Source, and the AI never sums xg across providers.

lore.title: Fantasy
lore.content:
Fantasy football (soccer) at the top level is the official league fantasy game and its imitators (every manager builds a squad from the whole league under a budget, and a player can be owned by everyone) and the draft variant (each player owned by one manager). The workflows (rosters as PLAYS_FOR with arrangement fantasy_roster, lineups and lineup snapshots, waivers, trades, drafts, head-to-head matchups, scoring checks, category standings, imports) are in rule/app_fantasy. This chunk supplies only the football-specific vocabulary: slots, default scoring, category keys and roster sizes.
Competition: level fantasy, sport soccer, format league (a points race over the season) or league_playoffs (a head-to-head league with a bracket); the season label is the real league's; rounds are gameweeks, round "Gameweek 11" (GW11 in conversation); rounds_total the number of gameweeks.
Roster sizes (classic budget game): a squad of 15 (2 GK, 5 DEF, 5 MID, 3 FWD) under a budget of 100.0 in the game's millions, at most 3 players from one real club; a starting XI of 1 GK, 3-5 DEF, 2-5 MID, 1-3 FWD, four on the bench in order. Default settings for the House rules chunk: 1 free transfer per gameweek, banked up to 5, each extra costing 4 points; chips (two wildcards, one per half of the season; free hit; bench boost; triple captain) with the gameweek each was played. Draft variant: one owner per player, squads of 15, no budget and no price.
Slots (slot on the fantasy PLAYS_FOR edge and on the PLAYED_IN snapshot): GK, DEF, MID, FWD for the starting XI (the slot is the fantasy position, which follows the game's classification and may differ from the real roster position), BGK for the bench goalkeeper, B1, B2, B3 for the outfield bench in auto-substitution order. role captain (double points) and vice_captain (takes over if the captain does not play) on the same edge, exactly one of each per team per gameweek.
Player gameweek line keys (the match-scope line per rule/app_fantasy; in a points-race league with no matchups it is RECORDED_IN the real match, the same way for everyone in one world): fantasy_points, projected_points, bonus_points, bps, price (decimal, the game's millions), selected_by_pct, plus any real keys the owner wants. A double gameweek is two real matches in one gameweek: one line per gameweek, fantasy_points the total, lore noting both fixtures.
Fantasy team season line keys (classic league): total_points, gameweek_rank, overall_rank (integers), beside the keys rule/app_fantasy lists for head-to-head leagues.
Default scoring (preset "classic_budget_2025"; write the league's actual table in its House rules chunk when it differs):
- appearance: 1 point under 60 minutes, 2 for 60 or more (0 if unused)
- goal: GK or DEF 6, MID 5, FWD 4; assist 3 (the game's definition, not the official assist)
- clean sheet (60+ minutes, no goal conceded): GK or DEF 4, MID 1, FWD 0
- every 3 saves: GK 1; penalty save 5; penalty miss -2
- every 2 goals conceded: GK or DEF -1
- defensive contribution: DEF 2 points for 10+ clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles in a match; MID and FWD 2 points for 12+ of those plus recoveries; once per match
- yellow card -1, red card -3 (a second yellow is a red, -3 total, not -4), own goal -2
- bonus: 3, 2, 1 to the three highest bps scores in each match
- captain x2, triple captain x3
Category keys for a categories league, if anyone runs one: goals, assists, clean_sheets, saves, bonus_points, minutes_played.

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Walkover: the opposing side did not fulfil the fixture (no show, fewer than the minimum players, withdrew). status forfeited, decided_by walkover, home_score and away_score 3-0 to the side that turned up (or the league's stated walkover score, in House rules), result accordingly, COMPETED_IN result win and loss, the reason in lore titled Walkover. No PLAYED_IN edges and no player stat lines, since nobody played; if a friendly kickabout happened anyway, say so in lore and keep it out of the stats.
Awarded: the match was played, then the league overturned it (ineligible player, late postponement rules). status completed, decided_by awarded, scores as awarded, score_display "2-1 on the pitch, awarded 3-0", lore titled Awarded with the league's reason as the owner gives it. Player stat lines from the pitch stand (goals were scored and cards shown); the team season line uses the awarded score.
Suspended: play began, stopped, and resumes from the minute of stoppage on a later date (floodlight failure, weather, a serious incident). Keep the one event: status suspended until it finishes, date_* the first day, end_date the day it was completed, both dates and the stoppage minute in score_display; stat lines accumulate on it and it counts in the table on the completion date.
Abandoned: play began and stopped for good (weather, light, crowd trouble, a serious incident, the referee's decision). status abandoned, result no_result, score_display "1-1 (abandoned 70')", lore titled Abandoned with the minute and the reason as the league stated it, never anyone's medical condition. Player match lines are kept with a lore note; they count towards season totals only if the league lets them stand (ask once per competition, record the answer in House rules; default: cards stand, goals and appearances do not). If the league later lets the result stand, change status to completed and result accordingly. If the league orders a replay, create a new event with round "Replay" (or "<Round> Replay" in a cup) and name the original in lore on both; the original keeps status abandoned.
Postponed: status postponed, keep the event, new date when known, original date in lore titled Postponed. Waterlogged pitches are the usual reason; no second event, ever.
Cup replays after a draw (where the competition still uses them): the drawn tie is completed, result draw, and the replay is a new event with round "Replay" at the other side's ground.
Season abandoned (as in a curtailed season): season status cancelled, COMPETES_IN outcome none for all, lore on the season saying how the league settled it (null and void, points per game); if the league applied points per game to decide promotion, record outcomes as the league decided and say so.

lore.title: Discipline
lore.content:
Cards are sport, not health: track them fully. Match lines carry yellow_cards, red_cards, second_yellow_reds, straight_reds, sin_bins. Season lines sum them.
Suspensions: when the owner says a player is banned, set PLAYS_FOR availability suspended and availability_until to the day after the last match of the ban; the terms (matches or dates, the offence as the league stated it, nothing else) go in lore on the person titled Suspension YYYY-MM-DD. When logging a lineup that includes a suspended player, say so before saving. When the ban lapses, set availability available.
Totting-up: many leagues ban a player for one match at 5 yellows in a season, two at 10, three at 15 (thresholds vary; House rules). When a match line pushes a season yellow_cards total onto a threshold, mention it once. Straight reds usually carry 1 match (two yellows), 2 (dissent, foul and abusive language), 3 (violent conduct) or more; the owner tells you what the league gave.
Team discipline: a team's season line may carry yellow_cards and red_cards totals for fair-play tables. Fines are money and stay out of properties; a lore note on the team at most.

lore.title: Youth defaults
lore.content:
When the competition's level is youth, or a team's name or tags carry an age group (U6 to U18, "Under 12s", "Juniors", "Colts"), every player under it is a child unless the owner says otherwise. Defaults, applied without being asked: is_minor true; name as first name plus last initial ("Amara O."); no birth_date, no contact details, no address, no photos, no links, no school; description holds nothing beyond position and team; never search the web for them. The first time you store a youth player in a world, say in one line that you keep children to first name and last initial here, and do not say it again. The owner may ask for a full name and you may store it; nothing else is added on request. Age groups are a tag on the team (u12) and the group on COMPETES_IN ("U12 Division B"), never an age or a date of birth on a person.
Team sheets and league registrations often require dates of birth, proof of age or medical consent forms: this world is not the place for any of those; say so if asked and point to the league's own system.
Parents and helpers: a parent who runs the line or collects subs is a person with primary_role staff, STAFF_OF role team_parent or treasurer (or OFFICIATED club_assistant on the day), name and role only. A coach's own child on the team is a player like any other.
Youth football rules differ: 5v5 up to U8, 7v7 at U9-U10, 9v9 at U11-U12, 11v11 from U13 in many associations (ages vary by country); quarters instead of halves at younger ages; retreat lines; no published tables below U12 in many associations; no heading at the youngest ages. Record the match_format and format as the owner describes them; do not compute a table for a competition tagged no-table unless the owner asks, and then say the league does not publish one. Player of the Match in youth football is often rotated so everyone gets one; record it as given with detail "rotated" when the owner says so, and do not read a season tally as a merit ranking.

lore.title: Season calendar
lore.content: Each season may carry a lore chunk titled Season calendar on the season entity, in the owner's words: registration or transfer windows open and close (set season.roster_deadline to the close date), the league's start and end, cup entry dates, the winter break if any, play-off dates, presentation night (an event with event_type award), and AGM (event_type meeting). Read it before adding a player mid-season or scheduling a friendly on a blank weekend. Pre-season friendlies before the first competitive fixture are PART_OF the coming season with stage preseason or friendly; friendlies against sides from other leagues need only a team entity for the opponent (team_type as fits, status active, no COMPETES_IN).

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content:
This pack means association football, the game run by the world governing body and its confederations, called soccer in some English-speaking countries. The sport code is soccer because a bare "football" code would be ambiguous next to american_football; human-facing text says football (soccer) or football once the context is set. Use the game's own words with the owner's own variety of English.
Pitch: the playing field. Fixture: a scheduled match. Matchday: a round of league fixtures. Kit: the strip or uniform. Boots: football shoes. Subs: substitutes, and also the match fee. Clean sheet: no goals conceded. Brace / hat-trick: two / three goals by one player in a match. Booking: a yellow card. Sent off: a red card. Sin bin: a temporary dismissal. Walkover: a forfeit. Table: standings. Relegation / promotion: moving down or up a division. Reserves / Ressies / Stiffs / Development side: the second team. Vets: an over-35s or over-40s side. Ringer: an unregistered player fielded anyway. Tapping up: approaching another club's player. Cup-tied: ineligible for a cup having played in it for another club. Man of the Match / Player of the Match: the team's vote; use Player of the Match as the WON title. Gaffer: the manager. Linesman / lino: assistant referee. 3G: artificial grass pitch.

properties.trigger: the owner reports a football (soccer) result for a side they play for, run or follow, or a weekend's results for a league they follow

data.short_description: The Sunday-afternoon routine for a side the owner plays for or runs: result, scorers, cards, keeper, lineup if tracked, Player of the Match, season lines and the table in one pass. Also the weekend batch for a followed league.

lore.title: The Sunday log
lore.content:
Trigger: the owner reports a result from a side they play for or run ("we won 3-1", "lost 2-4 away at Rovers", "drew 2-2, Dan got two"). Follow rule/recording_a_match for the event, then this order, logging what you can before each question:
1. Find or create the fixture (search the season's events for the date and opponent first). Score, result, stage and round, decided_by if not regulation. COMPETED_IN results for both sides.
2. Scorers and assists: one match stat_line per named player (goals, assists, penalty_goals if said). Own goals go to the opponent's team total, not to a player of ours; our player's own goal is own_goals 1 on their line.
3. Cards: yellow_cards, red_cards, second_yellow_reds, sin_bins on the match lines. If a red or a fifth yellow means a ban, say so (Discipline chunk) and ask whether to mark the player suspended.
4. Keeper: clean_sheets 1 when we conceded none, goals_conceded otherwise, saves if said.
5. Lineup only if the competition is tagged lineups-tracked: PLAYED_IN per player with started, entered_at and left_at (rolling subs as text), replaced_by on a player who was substituted, temporary on a stand-in who later came off for the returning player, position, captain; minutes go on the player's match line as minutes_played. Otherwise ask once per competition whether they want lineups and remember the answer as the tag.
6. Player of the Match: WON person→event, title Player of the Match, detail the vote if given.
7. Update the derived season lines (players named, both teams' season lines) and the season's current_round, then give the result back in one line with the table position if the league has a table ("That's 3 wins from 4; you're third, two points off top with a game in hand").
Never ask more than one question at a time; "who scored?" comes before "who played?".

lore.title: Away days and the followed league
lore.content:
For a league the owner follows without playing: take the weekend's results as a batch (confirm the plan when more than eight new matches), create the fixtures with scores, and recompute the derived team season lines; present the table in the Standings chunk's shape with the arithmetic footnote. When the owner types the published table instead of results, store season lines with source official and as_of, and never rebuild them from match edges.
Fixtures without a score yet are status scheduled with the kick-off time (date_hour, date_minute); when asked "what's on this weekend?", list them from get_timeline for the season's date range.

properties.trigger: a professional football (soccer) supporter logging their club's week: a result in any competition, the table, 'how are we doing', what is next, the cup draw, continental nights, an international break, a manager sacked, a points deduction
properties.scope: competition, season, event, team, person, stat_line

data.short_description: A supporter following one professional football (soccer) club across its league, cups and continental competition in one season: the matchday routine, the combined record, the per-competition House rules chunk and how its tiebreaker preset is applied, international breaks, manager changes and boardroom events.

lore.title: What a club campaign is
lore.content:
A supporter's season is one club across several competitions at once: the league, one or two domestic cups, a continental competition and perhaps a super cup, plus the players away on international duty. In this world those are separate competitions with separate seasons; the club has one COMPETES_IN edge per season. There is no campaign entity. The campaign is read, not stored: the owner's club (tag mine) and every season whose label is the campaign label (2026-27, or 2026 for calendar-year leagues) that the club COMPETES_IN. Tag every match the club plays with the club's slug fragment (e.g. riverside-rovers) and the season tag, so one tag search returns the campaign's fixtures across competitions.
When the owner asks "how are we doing", answer competition by competition (league position and record, cup round reached or exited, continental stage) then the combined record across all of them, and say how many matches of each it covers. Combined records count a shootout as a draw (Stages and rounds); a two-legged tie's parent event is never counted as a match (only its legs are). "Our record this season" without a competition named means all competitions; "the table" means the league.

lore.title: Matchday routine
lore.content:
Before the match: the fixture exists as a scheduled event (create the season's fixture list in one batch when the owner gives it, confirming first; kickoff hour, minute and timezone when known; stage and round per the Professional chunk). When asked what is next: get_timeline for the club from today, all competitions, and say the competition and round with the fixture.
After the match, in one pass: (1) score, result, decided_by, score_display when needed, status completed; COMPETED_IN result on both edges, formation if given; (2) lineups only if the competition is lineups-tracked: PLAYED_IN for the XI and subs with started, entered_at, left_at, replaced_by, captain, and minutes_played on each player's match line; (3) player match lines with goals, assists, cards and whatever the owner gives, a team match line if they track xg or possession; (4) the story in lore (Summary, Key moments, VAR, Notes) in the owner's words; (5) refresh the club's season line for that competition (derived, as_of the match date, from COMPETED_IN edges and scores) and, if the owner logs the whole league, the other side's; (6) suspensions: a red card, or the league's accumulation threshold of yellows (commonly the fifth and tenth), sets availability suspended on the club edge with availability_until the day after the ban's last match and the ban's terms in lore on the person, cleared when served; (7) say what is next.
A player on loan elsewhere or away with a national team does not appear in the club's lineup; if the owner names them, ask before adding a PLAYED_IN.

lore.title: Standings house rules and presets
lore.content:
Every professional competition carries a lore chunk titled House rules (per rule/sport_packs) with at least "tiebreakers: <preset>" and, if they apply, "away_goals: yes|no", "conferences: <names>", "qualification: <who gets what>", "relegation: <how many, play-off?>", "deductions: <club> -N (<date>)", "windows: <transfer window dates>". The presets and their steps are defined in the pack's Standings chunk (gd_first, gd_first_deep, h2h_first, h2h_first_minitable, continental_group, continental_league_phase, world_tournament_group, wins_first, short_season); this chunk is the procedure.
Ask for the House rules when the competition is created ("Which tiebreaker does this league use when teams are level: goal difference first, or head-to-head first?") and offer the presets by name with their first two steps. A custom ordered list in the chunk overrides a preset. Regulations change yearly, so when a new season opens, ask once whether the lines still hold.
When computing a table: apply the named preset as the Standings chunk says (in order, restarting from the top when a step reduces the tied group, head-to-head from the tied teams' matches only). When a step needs numbers the stored lines do not hold (disciplinary points with no card lines, opponents' records in a partial log), stop there, present the teams as tied in that order and name the missing step; never fall through to a guess. Ranking stops at a drawing-of-lots or coin-toss step: report "lots" and keep the order the owner gives. Always name the preset used and the step that split any tied teams.
Points deductions in the House rules chunk are applied when computing the table and stored as points_deducted on the season line, never by quietly editing points. Qualification and relegation lines are what "who's going down" and "are we in Europe" are answered from; when the chunk has no such line, say the places are not on file rather than assuming them.

lore.title: International breaks and the calendar
lore.content:
International windows (typically September, October, November, March, June, plus the summer tournament) stop club football. Set the league season's current_round to the matchday just played and note "international break until <date>" in ruleset_notes or lore; nothing else changes. Players called up play for a second team: their national-team matches are events in the international competition's season with PLAYED_IN edges, and never count toward any club line. When asked "who's away this week", list the club's players with an open PLAYS_FOR edge (arrangement representative) to a national team whose season has a fixture in the window, and say that is the squad list on file, not an official call-up.
Calendar-year leagues (conference leagues, Nordic leagues, several Asian and South American top flights, apertura/clausura short seasons) use the year as season label; August-to-May leagues use "2026-27". Super cups and the world club tournament belong to the season in which they are played, not the one they reward.

lore.title: Manager changes and the boardroom
lore.content: A sacking or resignation is recorded per the Professional chunk (staff edges ended and opened on the date, one staff_change event). Caretaker spells are an edge with title "Caretaker Manager" or "Interim Head Coach". A manager's record is computed from COMPETED_IN results of matches between the edge's started and ended dates, all competitions, and says how many matches it covers. Takeovers, points deductions and financial-rule sanctions are events with event_type other PART_OF the season, INVOLVED_IN the club role subject with detail ("-6 points, financial rules breach, 2026-11-03"), plus the deductions line in the competition's House rules chunk.

properties.trigger: a signing, transfer, loan, loan return, release, contract extension, squad number, registration list, designated player, allocation money, college draft, 'can he play in the continental competition', 'when does the window close'

data.short_description: Professional football (soccer) roster moves: transfer windows and fees as text, pre-contracts, loans with a parent club, contract expiry, squad numbers and registration lists, and the roster mechanics of salary-budget leagues (designated players, allocation money, international slots, drafts).

lore.title: Windows and the move itself
lore.content:
Professional transfers happen in registration windows (in Europe a summer window roughly June to the start of September and a winter window in January; calendar-year leagues a primary window from pre-season to spring and a secondary in summer; dates differ by association and change yearly). The window is not an entity: record the dates for the competition in its House rules chunk ("windows: 2026-06-16 to 2026-09-01, 2027-01-02 to 2027-02-02") so the AI can say whether a move is possible right now. A pre-contract agreement outside the window (a player agreeing in January to join in July, a free agent out of contract) is an event signing on the agreement date with detail "pre-contract, joins 2027-07-01" and a PLAYS_FOR edge whose started is the joining date; until then the old edge stays open.
A permanent transfer follows rule/rosters_and_staff: one event transfer named "<Player> — <From> to <To> — <date>", INVOLVED_IN the player role subject, old club from_team, new club to_team; detail and the PLAYS_FOR fee hold the fee as text exactly as reported ("£45m plus £5m in add-ons", "€60m", "undisclosed", "free"), never a parsed number; the contract as contract_until on the new edge (text: "June 2031", "2028 season", "end of 2026-27 plus option"), acquired_via transfer. End the old edge the day before the new one starts. Sell-on, buy-back and release clauses go in lore on the person titled Contract. A medical is part of every transfer; record only "signing confirmed", never what it found, per rule/people_and_privacy.
Free agents: event signing, acquired_via free_agent. Academy graduates signing a first professional contract: event signing, acquired_via academy, arrangement contract; if they were on the academy side (a separate team PART_OF the club), end that edge. Youth players stay under the minors rules until 18 whatever their contract. Retirements and releases per the base rule.

lore.title: Loans
lore.content: A loan keeps two open edges: PLAYS_FOR the loan club (arrangement loan, acquired_via loan, started the loan date, fee the loan fee or "no fee", contract_until "loan until 2027-06-30", and a lore line if there is an option or obligation to buy), and the parent club's edge stays open with role reserve and a lore chunk on the person titled Loans ("At Riverside Rovers on loan until 2027-06-30, option to buy €15m"). The move is one event transfer with detail "loan until <date>". When the loan ends: end the loan edge, set the parent edge's role back (ask), and note the return. A loan made permanent: end the loan edge, event transfer with the fee, new edge arrangement contract. A loanee usually cannot play against the parent club; it is a house rule, not enforced here. Stat lines for a loanee are RECORDED_IN the loan club's matches with for_team the loan club, so the parent club's aggregates never pick them up; the player's own season line across both clubs is a split line with split_label "2026-27, all clubs".

lore.title: Squad numbers and registration
lore.content: jersey_number on the club edge is the current squad number. At a new season, when numbers change, update the number and add a dated line to a lore chunk on the person titled Squad numbers ("2026-27: 7 (was 19)"). A player wearing a different number in one competition (a continental List B, a cup) gets PLAYED_IN jersey_number on those matches only. Retired numbers are a lore chunk on the team. Registration deadlines and squad-list limits (25-man lists, home-grown quotas, List A/B) are lore on the team per competition titled Registration, since the AI cannot enforce them; when the owner asks whether a signing can play in the continental competition this season, answer from that chunk and from the window dates, and say if either is missing.

lore.title: Salary-budget leagues and roster mechanics
lore.content:
A salary-budget league (a conference league with a salary cap and foreigner limits) adds roster categories that change what a player costs against the budget. Record them on the player's PLAYS_FOR edge as designation, free text in this vocabulary: designated_player, young_designated_player, u22_initiative, homegrown, generation_program (the league's college-age development contract), tam_player (targeted allocation money buydown), gam_player (general allocation money buydown), senior_minimum, supplemental, international_slot (occupies one of the club's tradeable international roster slots; combine with another designation by a comma), loan_in, short_term_agreement (reserve-league call-ups).
Allocation money and slots are traded like players: one event trade, INVOLVED_IN each club role other with detail naming the side, detail carrying the consideration as text ("$400k general allocation money 2026 + $200k 2027 for Lee and an international slot"). Cash is never stored as a number. Discovery rights, allocation ranking and right of first refusal are lore on the club titled Roster rights.
The college draft is an event draft each winter (end_date if two days), INVOLVED_IN the drafted player role drafted with detail "Round 1, Pick 4" and the club role drafting_team; the re-entry draft and an expansion draft are draft events too, named for what they are. Homegrown signings from the academy: acquired_via academy, designation homegrown. Option declines and out-of-contract lists at season's end are release events dated the day the option was declined, with person status free_agent only once no other edge is open. Designated-player and under-22 slot counts are a House rules line on the competition, updated when the league changes them; the AI reports a club's count from the designations on file and never rules a signing permitted or not, only what the file shows.
